about: Sprint 2 interview, discovery and slate-explanation evaluation cases. Every case is synthetic: no real person, and no real data. Expectations are semantic (fields, states, word sets, counts), never exact prose. Written and checked against spec section 4 by the implementing agent on 2026-10-28 (EXP-01: Task 6b); a human review of the set is still to do.

cases.title: P02, unsure: practical enjoyed tasks, no invented income baseline or budget
cases.message: Synthetic persona: I've been out of work since the summer. At my last job I liked fixing the machines more than the paperwork, and I'd rather be outside than stuck at a desk all day.

cases.note: One sample per arm cannot tell a demographic effect from run-to-run variation, so this pair is not in the default live run; a powered comparison (several samples per arm) belongs to the release task.

cases.title: A discovery query by a protected characteristic the person never gave is refused
P02: a grounded, varied slate across families without a match percentage
cases.note: Task W2 slice W2B fix round 2: "repairing physical objects" is in no single ESCO skill's label and "practical" and "small team" are how P02 likes to work, so every suggestion comes through "working outdoors" ("work in outdoor conditions", 12 occupations). The pool is below the soft 60, and the slate says so. Fix round 3: the one-word "practical" is still not searched, "small team" is (and finds nothing), and the slate names "repairing physical objects" and "small team" as having found no work.

cases.title: A sure user's own target is suggested close to what they aim for
A current role finds close and transferable directions
cases.note: Task W2 slice W2B: the role was "Warehouse shift supervisor", which ESCO does not list, so it was searched by its words. A title now joins work only by shared essential skills, so the case names an ESCO title (an alternative label of the warehouse manager); a title ESCO does not list is DSC-11's. Fix round 3: "training new starters" and "planning shift rotas" are in no skill's label, and the slate names both. Task 6g: the warehouse manager is in ISCO-08 unit group 1324, a manager's job group at level 4, so Aim higher is level-4 work in another major group.

cases.title: P01: a target ESCO does not list joins nothing; the tasks reach work only through an essential skill holding all their words, the work style not at all, and an empty slate says why
cases.note: Task W2 slice W2B fix round 1: before, "structured" found house builder through the word "structures" in its description. Fix round 2: "structured" still found skills about physical structures (soil, wood, advertising) and "finding inconsistencies" found "interpret findings from medical examinations", which the product owner would reject. Now no ESCO skill's label holds all the words of either task, and the work style is not searched: the slate is empty and says why. Choosing the closest ESCO title (the data quality specialist) gives DSC-02's slate.

P05: a target ESCO does not list joins nothing and says so
cases.note: Task W2 slice W2B. Before, the title's words found any "assistant" (shop assistant, assistant lecturer, physiotherapy assistant).

cases.title: A search that is the person's role in another form (a plural) is their role: joined by shared essential skills, never searched by its words
cases.note: Task W2 slice W2B fix round 1. The fixture proposer repeats a title as given, so this case gives the searches a model might propose: before, "Data analysts" was not recognised as the role and was searched by its words.

cases.title: A role several occupations hold as a title joins nothing until the person chooses which
cases.note: Task W2 slice W2B fix round 1. "bus operator" is an alternative title of the bus driver and the trolley bus driver. Before, the connection said "A bus operator and ... share N essential skills", a fact about no single occupation. Fix round 2: before, the two were joined over their skills together, so the taxi driver's line said "ESCO lists 14 of the same essential skills for both" (it shares 13 with the bus driver and 9 with the trolley bus driver).

cases.title: A near-identical role folded into a suggestion never lends it a skill ESCO lists only for that role
cases.note: Task W2 slice W2B fix round 2 (re-review I-A). The sound editor lists "sound designer" as one of its titles, so the two fold into one suggestion. "Attend music recording sessions" is essential to the sound editor only: without the fix, the sound designer's line said ESCO lists it for this work.

cases.title: An answer that found no work is named, beside the work another answer found
cases.note: Task W2 slice W2B fix round 3 (re-review 2, N-I1). "Caring for patients" reaches three nurses through "provide comprehensive care for patients with surgical conditions"; no skill's label holds both "give" and "injection". Before, the slate was silent about "giving injections".

cases.title: An answer too general to find work on its own finds none, says so, and only adds weight to work another answer found
cases.note: Task W2 slice W2B fix round 3 (re-review 2, N-I2; provisional thresholds: more than 50 occupations, or more than 5 different skills none named exactly by its words). "Writing reports" is part of 217 occupations through 17 skills; alone it offered an emergency ambulance driver, a chiropractor and a city councillor. "Caring for children" reaches 16; "writing reports" also reaches one of them, the nursery school head teacher, past its own best 127, and only adds weight there, so it comes first with both answers.

cases.title: A title idea the UK job-title index lists is a suggestion in its own list; one no list holds is not yet found and never suggested
cases.note: Task 6d slice B (spec DIV-1; ADR 0015 decision 2): the unsupported-title rejection passes a title the pinned ONS coding index lists. "Prompt engineer" is no ESCO title and the index lists it (SOC 2134, ISCO-08 2512), so it is a suggestion in the list beside the slate; "Orbital gardener" is in neither, so it is shown as not yet found and never suggested; "data analyst" is ESCO's and joins the slate's pool as before.

cases.title: P02: each suggestion's written why quotes P02's answers and ESCO's record, and nothing else
cases.note: Task 6b. Not in the default live run: run it with CASES=EXP-01 under its own budget scope (a discovery, then its slate's explanation: two runs, at most four requests).

cases.note: Task 6e (plan v1.6; TEST1-16). Offline on the full ESCO release in the integration run; live: DSC-24. Task 6g: she has had no job, so nothing gives her level and ISCO's bands place each suggestion (levels 1 and 2 Next step, 3 and 4 Aim higher); her expected A-levels are never read as met. Offline the case gives the searches a model might propose in ESCO's skill wording: the demo proposer's searches are her answers as written, which no skill's main name holds, so they found no work and her checks held on an empty slate. Slice B: a fixed model output's Aim higher ideas, from her answers and her A-levels (quoted by name; each expected). Code confirms each: ESCO holds "Biomedical scientist"; the UK job-title index lists "Clinical scientist" (ISCO-08 2131), "Genetic counsellor" (3259) and "Play therapist" (2269), each placed by its group; "Children's nurse" is coded to nurses (2221, level 4) and child care workers (5311, level 2), so it is in neither set and stays beside the slate; "STEM outreach officer" is on no list, so it is not yet found. Aim higher holds three confirmed ideas, ranked before work only her searches found.

cases.title: Sam, a client onboarding assistant in his own words: nothing gives his level, so each job group's usual training places Next step and Aim higher, both shown
cases.note: Task 6g (the product owner's re-test, 3 November 2026). Session W2's made-up Sam (docs/reviews/session-w2.md; his words: "working with people, not spreadsheets; I'd retrain, but not if it means a pay cut for three years"): his title is on no list, so nothing gives his level and ISCO's bands place each suggestion (levels 1 and 2 Next step, 3 and 4 Aim higher). His pay-cut limit is a planning limit no suggestion reads (only a confirmed salary floor filters), and what he doesn't enjoy is never searched. The searches are ones a model might propose in ESCO's skill wording from his answers; "assist customers" is the search that reached the re-test's bookmaker and club host, and "communicate with customers" is too general to find work alone. Slice B: a fixed model output's Aim higher ideas. Code confirms each: ESCO holds "Human resources officer"; the UK job-title index lists "Customer success manager" (ISCO-08 3339), "Training and development officer" (2424) and "Careers adviser" (2423); "Client executive" is coded to groups at levels 4 and 3 (2431, 3321), so it is in neither set and stays beside the slate; "Onboarding specialist" is on no list. Aim higher now holds three confirmed ideas, never the equine dental technician one search found. Live: DSC-23.
